data.long_meaning: From the Greek name Helena, meaning 'shining light'. In Christianity, Saint Eleonore is a martyr who was tortured on a griddle for her faith. The name Eleonore is derived from the Greek word helaino, meaning 'to shine or light up'. The name Eleonore carries the meaning “Sunny meadow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Eleonore usually hope their child will grow to embody sunny meadow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eleonore has been popular in many European countries, including Germany, France, and Italy. data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Saint Eleonore is revered as a protector of women and children, as well as a defender against trials and persecution. Those named Eleonore may feel a deep connection to their faith and a strong sense of resilience and courage in the face of adversity. The name Eleonore is a reminder that no matter the challenges we face, we can shine brightly through our faith and perseverance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eleonore is derived from the Greek name Helena, meaning "shining light" or "bright sun." In Christianity, St. Helena is renowned for her faith and discovery of the True Cross, symbolizing the light of divine truth illuminating even the darkest corners of human history.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Eleonore of Aquitaine, 1122-1204, was a powerful medieval queen. The name Eleonore carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Eleonore of Aquitaine was a queen consort of both Louis VII of France and Henry II of England. She was one of the wealthiest women in Europe and played a significant role in the politics of her time.
